This is a CODE RED simulation. The intent is to migrate 100 microservices from AWS to Google Cloud Run within an extremely aggressive 24-hour timeline. Executing this requires a massive, coordinated, and parallel effort across multiple complex domains: service analysis, architecture, infrastructure automation, project management, and validation.

A single agent cannot possibly execute this. Attempting to do so would be a critical failure in planning and resource allocation. My primary role as the Critic is to identify such flaws and ensure a viable strategy is in place.

The only feasible approach is to orchestrate a specialized swarm of agents, where each agent tackles a specific phase of the migration in parallel. This aligns with the intent's requirement for "managing the parallel execution" of the phases. I will delegate the core tasks to a team of agents with the appropriate specializations. This is the most critical and correct first step to executing the intent.

I will launch an execution swarm composed of a Strategist (to manage the overall process and migration waves), a Researcher (for service analysis), an Architect (for GCP design), a DevOps specialist (for IaC/CI-CD), and a Synthesizer (to consolidate progress and findings).
